story: Students join the AI Creators Guild, a studio that takes on fun creative missions. Each module is a Quest Line that ends with a Boss Challenge (the final project). Students earn XP for good learning habits (trying, fixing, helping), not just for talent. They level up from Prompt Rookie to AI Architect and collect badges. In a group, four Houses compete, and house scores use the average so team size doesn't matter. 1-on-1, the student plays against the teacher ('Team Bolt') and against their own best score. The same system runs all year, so students always know how to move up.

xpRules.notes: Trying counts. Any honest try earns it.
Each lesson's build has 1 or 2 checkpoints.
Group: every member of the winning house, and 5 XP to every house that finishes. 1-on-1: the student gets 15 for playing and 5 more for beating Team Bolt.
Using 'I like / I wonder / Try'. 1-on-1: feedback on the teacher's work counts too!
Extra quests for students who finish early, or for homework.
Catching a real AI mistake or unfair pattern and proving it with a source.
Rubric score 1 to 4 on each row. Up to 100 XP.
An extra hard add-on to the final project.

levels.name: Prompt Rookie
levels.perk: Guild nickname + avatar (made with AI in Launch).

levels.name: Story Weaver
levels.perk: Pick the subject for one build.

levels.name: Web Smith
levels.perk: Your work goes on the showcase wall.

levels.name: Flow Builder
levels.perk: Become a Guild Helper: teach a skill to someone else.

levels.name: Game Designer
levels.perk: Skip one exit ticket (still do the build!).

levels.name: AI Architect

badges.name: Safety Pact
badges.how: Signed the AI Safety Pact and passed the safety quiz.

badges.name: Prompt Duelist
badges.how: Finished the Launch Boss: Prompt Duel.

badges.name: Pixel Forger
badges.how: Finished a whole Brand Kit (Images Boss).

badges.name: Hook Master
badges.how: Finished an AI video with an AI label (Video Boss).

badges.name: Web Smith
badges.how: Put a landing page + store online (Web Boss).

badges.name: Flow Builder
badges.how: Built a working AI helper (Agents Boss).

badges.name: Fact Checker
badges.how: Caught 3 real AI mistakes and proved them with sources.

badges.name: Ethics Guardian
badges.how: Spoke up kindly about asking first, copying or honesty.

badges.name: Guild Mentor
badges.how: Helped 5 people get unstuck without touching their keyboard. 1-on-1: taught a skill to a family member or friend.

badges.name: Bug Hunter
badges.how: Found and fixed a bug by explaining it clearly to the AI.

badges.name: Iteration Station
badges.how: Showed 5 or more saved tries of one piece of work.

badges.name: On a Roll
badges.how: Did 10 exit tickets in a row.

rituals.name: Recall Raid
rituals.how: 5 quick questions that mix THIS module with older ones. Group: houses answer on whiteboards. 1-on-1: rapid fire, out loud.
rituals.principle: Pulling old ideas back out of memory makes them stick much better than reading them again.

rituals.name: Prompt of the Week
rituals.how: Show the best prompt from last week and take it apart with the Prompt Recipe. 1-on-1: use the student's own best prompt.
rituals.principle: Seeing a good example from someone like you shows what 'good' looks like.

rituals.name: Spot the AI Mistake
rituals.how: Show an AI answer with a mistake in it. Find it and prove it with a source.
rituals.principle: Asking 'is this true, and how do I know?' builds careful thinking.

rituals.name: Gallery Walk / Show & Tell
rituals.how: Group: walk around and leave sticky notes (I like / I wonder / Try). 1-on-1: the student shows their work and you trade feedback both ways.
rituals.principle: Explaining and judging work helps you understand it better.

rituals.name: Boss Week
rituals.when: Last 1 or 2 lessons of each module
rituals.how: Finish the final project, then show it off and score it with the rubric. Beat the Boss = module badge.
rituals.principle: Using many skills together on one big project helps students use them later.

moduleHooks.questLine: Join the Guild: make your avatar, learn the rules of AI.
A made-up company hires the Guild to design its whole look.
The company needs a launch video that people really watch.
Give the brand a home on the internet and a store.
The studio is too busy. Build robot helpers!
Build an app for yourself — your own tool.
The Guild's arcade: remix a classic, then invent your own.
Show the world what the Guild built.

fairness: Most XP comes from effort (trying, fixing, helping), so every student can level up, not just the fastest.
Group: house scores use the AVERAGE XP per member, so uneven team sizes stay fair.
Group: show house scores to everyone, but show each student's XP privately, so no one feels bad.
1-on-1: the student competes with Team Bolt (you) and with their own best score. Let them win fair and square. Don't make it too easy.
Give XP right away with the tracker (2 clicks). Keep it fast. The game should never eat lesson time.
